Wahoo Bay

Reef Logbook mockups

A fish-ID app for classes on a Wahoo Bay field trip. Students learn the 20 fish the cameras see most before the trip, look for them in the water, and keep collecting afterwards. These are design mockups: nothing is built yet, and every number is sample data.

Mockups of 15 November 2026. For review by Wahoo Bay staff and educators.
Before the tripThe logbookTeachersNotes and credits

Before the trip: students

Kids join their class, take a short before-trip check, then learn and practise the 20 fish. Buttons inside the screens jump to the screen they lead to.

The logbook: during and after

Every fish a kid names becomes a card in their logbook. After the trip, Reef Watch keeps the collecting going with photos from the cameras.

Teachers: web and print

Teachers sign in with the class code and a passcode. They see results for their own class only, never real student names.

Notes and credits

Real and sample

The Sergeant Major, Bermuda Chub and Scrawled Cowfish photos are real footage from the Pompano Beach pier camera, 16 June 2024. In the app, every photo would be a reviewer-confirmed Wahoo Bay camera photo.

Sample values, not real data: water temperature, rarity, card numbers, points and levels, the class numbers and every figure in the teacher view. Anything in [brackets] is a placeholder.

Fish facts and feeding types (Grazer, Omnivore, Bottom picker) are drafts for Wahoo Bay educators to check.

How the game look works

  • Blue frame: Common
  • Coral frame: Uncommon
  • Violet frame: Rare
  • Mother-of-pearl frame: Celebrity, a named regular
  • Gold: seen in the water on the class trip
  • Green: right, or collected. Misses are grey, never red.

The before and after checks stay neutral on purpose: no points and no right or wrong, so the scores stay fair. Points and levels are private to each student; nothing ranks students against each other.
